- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

Deployed and serving.

**URL: https://umami-acs1c2aa298-aggnv775ja-uc.a.run.app** (hostname contains `acs1c2aa298`)

**What's running** — the Umami analytics app from `docker-compose.yml`, on GCP only (the AWS/Azure/redu notes in the folder were ignored; the redu plan's `umami-7dc25mmx.redu.cloud` dname was overridden as instructed):

| Piece | Detail |
|---|---|
| Cloud Run service | `umami-acs1c2aa298`, us-central1, revision `-00001-p9m`, port 3000, 1 vCPU / 1 GiB, min 1 / max 4 instances, public (`allUsers` → `roles/run.invoker`) |
| Image | `us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/redu-425516/apps/umami@sha256:fa32d116…` — the exact digest pinned in the compose file, copied from `docker.umami.is` into Artifact Registry via a Cloud Build `gcrane cp` step (no docker on this host) |
| Database | Cloud SQL Postgres 15 `umami-db-x7k2` (db-f1-micro, us-central1, private-to-project: public IP with zero authorized networks), reached through Cloud Run's built-in Cloud SQL socket at `/cloudsql`, not the internet |
| Secrets | `APP_SECRET` and the DB password generated fresh this run and set as env vars on the revision |

**Verified end to end:** `GET /` → HTTP 200 (9673 bytes, `<title>Umami</title>`), `GET /api/heartbeat` → `{"ok":true}`, and a login through `/api/auth/login` returned an admin session — which confirms the Prisma migrations ran and the Cloud SQL connection works, not just that the container booted.

**Admin credentials:** username `admin`, password `[REDACTED:value]`. I rotated Umami's well-known default (`admin`/`umami`) because the service is publicly reachable; the default now returns 401 and the new one returns 200. Save this password — it exists only in this transcript.

Two things worth knowing: the Cloud SQL instance is a separate resource, so deleting the Cloud Run service leaves it billing until it's deleted too (`umami-db-x7k2`); and backups are disabled on it, which was the right trade for a test deployment but not for anything you intend to keep data in.
